14.constraint: Use the lavender ribbed corduroy half-zip once only for Spring or Fall Casual Everyday, Date Night, or Travel. Pair with ecru, stone, controlled gray, or mid-blue straight bottoms and keep the remaining layers quiet.

26.constraint: Use the muted fruit-green regular drawstring short once only for Summer Casual Everyday, Travel, or Vacation / Resort. Pair with a clean white, ecru, pale-blue, or restrained striped regular-fit top and low-profile footwear.

rejectionGroups.reason: The loud multicolor stripe, patchwork, or paint-mark treatment reads novelty-led and supplier-generic rather than controlled modern shirting.
The sleeves and torso sit too close on the muscular model, the long curved hem is awkward, and the deep-open styling does not prove the relaxed modern fit required.
Hanger-only imagery, visible pseudo-brand labels or chest graphics, and accessory styling prevent trustworthy adult-male fit approval.
The color direction is potentially useful, but garment-only imagery does not prove shoulder, torso, sleeve, hem, or material behavior well enough for a unique wardrobe allocation.
The dropped shoulder, stacked sleeves, and long pooled hem create an uncontrolled oversized corduroy silhouette that also repeats an already stronger approved role.
The narrow torso, tight sleeves, deep-open chest, and cropped model framing recreate the skinny-shirt problem.
Shiny broken stripes, a hanger-only presentation, and visible underlayer text make the shirt busy and unproven.
Product-only imagery does not prove rise, thigh volume, length, or adult-male fit well enough for a one-time short allocation.
The external towel-retention loop dominates the back of the short and makes the product gimmicky and too specialized.
The long wide color-block construction is baggy, loud, and dated rather than clean modern sportswear.
Camouflage or tie-dye surfaces, visible text or labels, and product-only proof make the shorts noisy and supplier-generic.
The knee-length wide culotte proportion is shown on an ambiguously gendered fit and lacks the controlled men's short silhouette required.
The long loose cut and visible leg labels recreate the baggy branded-short problem.
Product-only or mannequin imagery, distressed or shiny synthetic surfaces, quilted panels, patches, contrast blocks, and dated trims fail the modern outerwear standard.
The narrow product-only cardigan shapes are long, dark, and fitted, with no adult on-body proportion proof.
Hanger-only proof plus contrast stitching, visible chest branding, or unresolved cardigan volume prevents approval.
The tie-front three-quarter-sleeve cardigan is excessively loose and paired with equally baggy bottoms, repeating the uncontrolled silhouette problem.
